summary: Herkimer County lookout from July 1910, steel tower from 1919, closed 1945, removed 1977 (or c.1985); Pepperbox Wilderness ridge, no remains described.

facts.design: All-steel lookout with an enclosed crow's nest (1942 survey); 1919 entries name a 60-foot Aermotor tower or a steel tower
facts.status_note: Tower and observer's cabin removed in 1977 (Forest Lookouts gives c.1985). No source describes the site today.

access.note: Pepperbox Wilderness, part of the Forest Preserve, with few official facilities; the tower site needs off-trail navigation to reach

visit.trail_note: Trailhead on Moshier Road near the Beaver River; the trails are faint and obscure

events.note: Log fire observation tower; lookout established in July 1910 at a cost of $308.39, per the Sixteenth Annual Report of the Forest, Fish and Game Commission
Steel structure replaced the log tower; one 1919 entry gives a 60-foot Aermotor tower, another a steel tower
Closed because of redundancies with other nearby towers
Refurbished after the 1950 windstorm (called a hurricane in the 2020 article); the revival of interest was brief
State employees removed the fire tower and observer's cabin; the Forest Lookouts page gives c.1985 instead

corrections.why: The brief's agency field holds a date fragment. The 1942 survey says the station is property of the New York Conservation Department.

corrections.proposed: not verified; sources place the ridge in Herkimer County, north of Threemile Beaver Meadow
corrections.why: The brief's coordinates sit near the New Jersey line, well south of Herkimer County, which the brief's own local_unit field and the sources both place it in.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1919 entries disagree: one says a 60-foot Aermotor tower, the other a steel tower. The 1942 survey says the all-steel lookout is about 30 feet high. The facts keep the 60-foot figure from the 1919 entry and the story reports the survey's figure without choosing.
The 2020 article and the Adirondack history both give 1977. The Forest Lookouts page gives c.1985. Facts use 1977, and the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Probable duplicate of us-ny-beaver-lake-mountain: same Herkimer County tower and same sources; merge candidate. The brief's coordinates are not in Herkimer County (see corrections). The -2 record's own source page is the Forest Lookouts page, which has no coordinates. The existing record's point (43.91558, -75.13617) was not checked against a map here. The 1945 closure and the mid-1950s closure both come from one source and are presented in sequence, not as conflict.
